title: Conormal modules of presentations of S and of a principal localization of S agree up to free summands
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ an $R$-algebra, $g\in S$ and $S_g$ the localization of $S$ at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Let $n,m\ge0$, let $\alpha:R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S$ and $\beta:R[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to S_g$ be surjective homomorphisms of $R$-algebras from polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $I=\ker\alpha$ and $J=\ker\beta$. Then $I/I^2$ is an $S$-module, $J/J^2$ is an $S_g$-module, and with $(I/I^2)_g$ the localization of the $S$-module $I/I^2$ at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] there is an isomorphism of $S_g$-modules $(I/I^2)_g\oplus S_g^{\oplus m}\cong J/J^2\oplus S_g^{\oplus n}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00S6 (lemma-conormal-module-localize, line 35776), whose proof uses Lemma 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL), Lemma 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy) and Lemma 00S5 (lemma-conormal-module, line 35761)

proof.text: (The two complexes and their terms.) Let $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $Q=R[y_1,\dots,y_m]$. Since $\alpha$ is surjective, $S\cong P/I$ and $I/I^2$ is an $P/I=S$-module; likewise $J/J^2$ is a $Q/J\cong S_g$-module. Write $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)$ for the two-term complex of $S$-modules $\mathrm d_\alpha:I/I^2\to S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$, $f\bmod I^2\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm df$, and $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)$ for $\mathrm d_\beta:J/J^2\to S_g\otimes_Q\Omega_{Q/R}$ ($\Omega$, $\mathrm d$ as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]). Let $K=\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)\otimes_SS_g$ be the complex $\mathrm d_K=\mathrm d_\alpha\otimes1:K_1=(I/I^2)\otimes_SS_g\to K_0=(S\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R})\otimes_SS_g=\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_PS_g$ of $S_g$-modules. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] (for the $P$-algebra $S_g$, via $P\to S\to S_g$, and for the $Q$-algebra $S_g$ via $\beta$), $K_0$ is a free $S_g$-module with basis $\mathrm dx_1\otimes1,\dots,\mathrm dx_n\otimes1$ and $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)_0=S_g\otimes_Q\Omega_{Q/R}$ is free with basis $1\otimes\mathrm dy_1,\dots,1\otimes\mathrm dy_m$; so $K_0\cong S_g^{\oplus n}$ and $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)_0\cong S_g^{\oplus m}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor] (ring $S$, element $g$, module $I/I^2$), $K_1=(I/I^2)\otimes_SS_g\cong(I/I^2)_g$ as $S_g$-modules [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S6 (lemma-conormal-module-localize), lines 35787-35798; definition of NL(alpha) in Section Tag 00S0, lines 35188-35206

proof.text: (The presentation $\beta'$ of $S_g$ built from $\alpha$.) Since $\alpha$ is surjective choose $f\in P$ with $\alpha(f)=g$. Let $P[x]=R[x_1,\dots,x_n,x]$ be the polynomial ring in one more variable and $\beta':P[x]\to S_g$ the homomorphism of $R$-algebras which is $\alpha$ followed by $S\to S_g$ on $P$ and sends $x$ to $1/g$; let $J'=\ker\beta'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-naive-cotangent] (with $A=R$, $B=S$, the presentation $\alpha$ on the variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$, the element $g$ and this $f$), $\beta'$ is surjective, and by its clause (3) there is an isomorphism of complexes of $S_g$-modules $\Theta:K\oplus C\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{NL}(\beta')$, where $C$ is the complex $S_g\xrightarrow{\ g\ }S_g$ and $\mathrm{NL}(\beta')$ is $\mathrm d_{\beta'}:J'/J'^2\to\Omega_{P[x]/R}\otimes_{P[x]}S_g$, $u\bmod J'^2\mapsto\mathrm du\otimes1$; i.e. $S_g$-linear isomorphisms $\Theta_1:K_1\oplus S_g\to J'/J'^2$, $\Theta_0:K_0\oplus S_g\to\Omega_{P[x]/R}\otimes S_g$ with $\mathrm d_{\beta'}\Theta_1=\Theta_0(\mathrm d_K\oplus g)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S6 (lemma-conormal-module-localize), lines 35787-35798 ('Let beta' : R[x_1,...,x_n,x] -> S_g be the presentation of Lemma 08JZ constructed starting with alpha. Then NL(alpha) (x)_S S_g is homotopy equivalent to NL(beta')'); Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL, line 35605) (3)

proof.text: ($K$ is homotopy equivalent to $\mathrm{NL}(\beta')$.) Put $u_i=\Theta_i\circ\iota_i:K_i\to\mathrm{NL}(\beta')_i$ and $v_i=\pi_i\circ\Theta_i^{-1}:\mathrm{NL}(\beta')_i\to K_i$ ($i=0,1$), where $\iota_i:K_i\to K_i\oplus S_g$, $a\mapsto(a,0)$, and $\pi_i:K_i\oplus S_g\to K_i$, $(a,c)\mapsto a$. Since $\iota,\pi$ commute with $\mathrm d_K\oplus g$ and $\Theta$ is an isomorphism of complexes, $\mathrm d_{\beta'}u_1=u_0\mathrm d_K$ and $\mathrm d_Kv_1=v_0\mathrm d_{\beta'}$. Clearly $v_iu_i=\pi_i\iota_i=\mathrm{id}_{K_i}$. Since $g$ is a unit of $S_g$, define $k:K_0\oplus S_g\to K_1\oplus S_g$, $(a,c)\mapsto(0,g^{-1}c)$. Then $k\circ(\mathrm d_K\oplus g)(a,c)=(0,c)$ on $K_1\oplus S_g$ and $(\mathrm d_K\oplus g)\circ k(a,c)=(0,c)$ on $K_0\oplus S_g$, i.e. both equal $\mathrm{id}-\iota_i\pi_i$. Conjugating by $\Theta$ and putting $H=\Theta_1k\Theta_0^{-1}:\mathrm{NL}(\beta')_0\to\mathrm{NL}(\beta')_1$: $\mathrm{id}-u_1v_1=\Theta_1(\mathrm{id}-\iota_1\pi_1)\Theta_1^{-1}=H\mathrm d_{\beta'}$ and $\mathrm{id}-u_0v_0=\mathrm d_{\beta'}H$. All maps are $S_g$-linear.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S6 (lemma-conormal-module-localize), lines 35787-35798; the splitting of the proof of Lemma Tag 08JZ, lines 35674-35688

proof.text: Let Q be the composite polynomial presentation of S_g constructed in step 2, and V the original presentation beta, both packaged as Generators. Mathlib's Generators.defaultHom gives lifts in both directions; Hom.toExtensionHom gives extension maps phi and psi. Their induced Cotangent.map and CotangentSpace.map commute with cotangentComplex by CotangentSpace.map_comp_cotangentComplex. Set h = (Hom.id Q.toExtension).sub (psi.comp phi) and h' = (Hom.id V.toExtension).sub (phi.comp psi). Apply Mathlib's Cotangent.map_sub_map and CotangentSpace.map_sub_map to these two pairs of maps, then simplify map_id and map_comp. This gives all four homotopy identities directly from the universal derivation [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], without importing the separate presentation-homotopy statement.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S6 (lemma-conormal-module-localize), lines 35787-35798 ('We know that NL(beta) and NL(beta') are homotopy equivalent by Lemma 00S1'); Lemma Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy, line 35274)

proof.text: (Composing the two homotopy equivalences.) Let $a_i=\varphi_iu_i:K_i\to\mathrm{NL}(\beta)_i$ and $b_i=v_i\psi_i:\mathrm{NL}(\beta)_i\to K_i$; they commute with the differentials ($\mathrm d_\beta a_1=\varphi_0\mathrm d_{\beta'}u_1=\varphi_0u_0\mathrm d_K=a_0\mathrm d_K$, and likewise $\mathrm d_Kb_1=b_0\mathrm d_\beta$). Since $v_iu_i=\mathrm{id}$ (step 3), $\mathrm{id}-b_ia_i=v_i(\mathrm{id}-\psi_i\varphi_i)u_i$; with step 4 and the chain-map identities this is $v_1h\mathrm d_{\beta'}u_1=(v_1hu_0)\mathrm d_K$ in degree $1$ and $v_0\mathrm d_{\beta'}hu_0=\mathrm d_K(v_1hu_0)$ in degree $0$. So $H_K:=v_1hu_0:K_0\to K_1$ satisfies $\mathrm{id}-b_1a_1=H_K\mathrm d_K$, $\mathrm{id}-b_0a_0=\mathrm d_KH_K$. Further $\mathrm{id}-a_ib_i=(\mathrm{id}-\varphi_i\psi_i)+\varphi_i(\mathrm{id}-u_iv_i)\psi_i$; by steps 3 and 4 this is $h'\mathrm d_\beta+\varphi_1H\mathrm d_{\beta'}\psi_1=(h'+\varphi_1H\psi_0)\mathrm d_\beta$ in degree $1$ and $\mathrm d_\beta h'+\varphi_0\mathrm d_{\beta'}H\psi_0=\mathrm d_\beta(h'+\varphi_1H\psi_0)$ in degree $0$. So $H_\beta:=h'+\varphi_1H\psi_0:\mathrm{NL}(\beta)_0\to J/J^2$ satisfies $\mathrm{id}-a_1b_1=H_\beta\mathrm d_\beta$, $\mathrm{id}-a_0b_0=\mathrm d_\beta H_\beta$. All these maps are $S_g$-linear.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00S6 (lemma-conormal-module-localize), lines 35787-35798 ('We conclude that NL(alpha) (x)_S S_g is homotopy equivalent to NL(beta)')

proof.text: (Conclusion.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-two-term-homotopy-equivalence-direct-sum] over the ring $S_g$ to $d_A=\mathrm d_K:K_1\to K_0$, $d_B=\mathrm d_\beta:J/J^2\to\mathrm{NL}(\beta)_0$, the maps $a_i$, $b_i$ and the homotopies $H_K$, $H_\beta$ of step 5: $K_1\oplus\mathrm{NL}(\beta)_0\cong J/J^2\oplus K_0$ as $S_g$-modules. By step 1, $K_1\cong(I/I^2)_g$, $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)_0\cong S_g^{\oplus m}$ and $K_0\cong S_g^{\oplus n}$, hence $(I/I^2)_g\oplus S_g^{\oplus m}\cong J/J^2\oplus S_g^{\oplus n}$ as $S_g$-modules.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks 00S6 (lemma-conormal-module-localize, algebra.tex 35776) and its proof, and the statements and proofs of 08JZ, 00S1, 00S3, 00S5 (tags verified in tags/tags). Statement kept (Stacks' 'finite type' hypothesis is implied by the finite presentations alpha, beta). Proof in six steps following 00S6: the complexes K = NL(alpha) (x)_S S_g and NL(beta) with free degree-0 terms of ranks n and m (Kahler basis node, localization-tensor node); the presentation beta' : R[x_1..x_n,x] -> S_g of 08JZ and the isomorphism NL(beta') = K (+) (S_g -g-> S_g) of its clause (3) (existing node); K homotopy equivalent to NL(beta') (elementary: g is a unit, so the summand is contractible); NL(beta') homotopy equivalent to NL(beta) (new node, 00S1); composition of homotopy equivalences written out (elementary); conclusion by the new node for 00S3. The source's last sentence 'apply Lemma 00S5' is read as the argument of 00S5's proof (00S1 + 00S3): 00S5 itself compares two presentations of one algebra and K is not the NL of a presentation; the route through 00S5 for beta', beta would need cancelling a free summand S_g, which fails in general. Two new unsplit nodes: lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentations-homotopy-equivalent (00S1, Mathlib candidate Extension.Hom.sub with map_sub_map recorded), lem-weil-pbc-two-term-homotopy-equivalence-direct-sum (00S3, no Mathlib match). Item re-searched (loogle, leanfinder, leansearch, local_search): not in Mathlib.
